wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Three days of Qatari-mediated talks in Doha have produced no deal, while the IRGC Navy claims two tankers hit mines on an 'unauthorized route' through Hormuz. Khamenei ordered commanders to answer any attack without geographic limits, and Axios's sources say Netanyahu pressed Trump to strike Iran after the midterms.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Over 30 attacks hit ships near Hormuz in October, a record, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed tankers ablaze on what they call an unauthorised route. OPEC+ left its December targets unchanged, and three days of Qatari-mediated talks in Doha produced no deal. In Maine, heating oil reached $6.05 a gallon.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The pressure on crude runs through the US-Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz, where over 30 attacks hit ships in October and the IRGC said it halted two tankers. Houthis claimed a strike on a Saudi refinery, OPEC+ left December targets unchanged, and heating oil in Maine reached $6.05 a gallon.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The gas crisis of the past fortnight played out overseas: strikes cut Iran's gas capacity by a fifth, European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour, and QatarEnergy agreed to buy US liquefied natural gas. None of it accounts for the moves in this price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: The fortnight's wheat news ran through the Black Sea and Pakistan: Zelensky said Turkey would help restore Ukraine's grain corridor, Rubio saw growing interest in a Black Sea ceasefire, and Pakistan raised its support price to Rs4,500 a maund amid a flour crisis. None of it accounts for the world price.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Demand tied to AI fuelled the boom: Chinese buyers paid a record $200-plus a ton above London prices at Yangshan. Supply tightened too, with Mysteel expecting China's fourth-quarter refined output to fall as smelters trim, and Rio Tinto's Oyu Tolgoi halting underground operations.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: The Fed held rates despite US inflation, yet markets fully priced a December hike, and a Reuters commentary said Warsh's muddled messaging had revived doubts about the Fed's credibility. The cost of higher yields reaches bank balance sheets: Bank of America's unrealized bond losses rose to $109 billion.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The Fed left interest rates unchanged despite inflation, and Bank of America's unrealized bond losses rose to $109 billion. Walmart and Eli Lilly joined 36 others objecting to tokenized shares of their stock. None of this accounts for the index's path over the period.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: Alphabet's quarterly capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion and its free cash flow turned negative, while Amazon's 12-month cash burn hit a record $42.4 billion. Anthropic's listing filing showed an $80.7 billion loss on $16.3 billion of revenue. All of it concerns the bill for AI, and none of it accounts for this price's path.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The Hormuz closure has left fuel markets short. Trump's deal with Putin to lower fuel prices sent 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel from Primorsk toward New York, too late for the Midterms, and Ukraine reportedly paused refinery strikes under US pressure before drones targeted Kstovo. These reports concern diesel, not gasoline.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour in October, its highest since 2022, as the Iran war reached the region's gas supply. Strikes cut Iran's gas capacity by a fifth, Qatar agreed to import up to 4 million tons of US gas a year, and the Qatari carrier Al Mayeda was hit in the Gulf.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: Diesel in Pakistan passed Rs400 a litre and imported gas rose 14% for Punjab and 15.27% for Sindh. Neither story ties those increases to the exchange rate, and nothing reported this fortnight accounts for the rupee's path.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: President Tinubu asked the Senate to approve external loans of $20.5 billion and €1.04 billion under a 2026-2027 borrowing plan, and OPay raised $304 million in a New York listing. Neither the loan request, which has not been reported as approved, nor the listing accounts for the exchange rate's path.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: Egypt's parliament voted behind closed doors to authorise defending Saudi Arabia during the Iran war, and Arab and Islamic countries called for traffic to resume through the Strait of Hormuz, but nothing reported ties either event to the pound.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey's recent news was diplomatic: Ankara submitted the Makkah defence pact for ratification, signed a partnership with Canada and won eastern Libya's vote for its 2019 maritime deal, while Zelensky said Turkey would help restore Ukraine's grain corridor. None of it accounts for the lira's price.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: Bangladesh formed a wage board on Sunday as garment workers in Ashulia and Gazipur kept protesting, demanding 30,000 taka a month, up from 12,500, in the sector that earns most of the country's exports. None of it accounts for the exchange rate's move.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: Jakarta stocks fell 11.6% in one Friday session, their worst day since 1998, under the threat of an MSCI downgrade, and Indonesia then announced new measures to improve stock market transparency. None of the reports ties that rout directly to the rupiah, and nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for its price.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: Lebanon's news this fortnight was of Israeli forces bulldozing olive groves at Kfarshouba, and of Palestinian refugees in the Beddawi camp in Tripoli squeezed by high energy prices and inflation. None of it accounts for the pound's price.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: Yuan borrowing abroad ran through the fortnight: Bank of China's 2 billion yuan bond in Dubai drew 5 times demand, and Afreximbank weighed a first yuan tranche on a $1 billion loan. Neither deal accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The RBI stepped in on the rupee in late October: likely central-bank dollar sales in Mumbai gave it a lift, in a story tied to oil prices and Brent. The month's other big Indian market event, the Jio Platforms listing, is not shown to have moved the currency.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: Lula's runoff win over Flávio Bolsonaro, the market's pick, sent real futures down 10%, with the fiscal deficit the sore point. Brazilian companies had already been moving into dollar stablecoins before the result. Bolsonaro then refused to concede a 4.4 million-vote loss and left for the US, where a Trump aide confirmed political asylum.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Inflation of 3.62% in early October ran above forecasts, the one recent report from Mexico that bears on its currency, but it does not account for the peso's slide.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour, its highest since 2022, raising the euro zone's import bill. France's 10-year bond yield reached 4.96%, Fitch cut its outlook after the economy shrank 0.1%, and ECB head Christine Lagarde is to step down in February. None of these reports ties the currency's move to any of it directly.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Doubts about AI sent money into the yen as a safe haven, while Treasury yields fell. The same boom also reaches Japan as a borrower's market: foreign issuers sold a record $16 billion of yen bonds from April to September, as AI hyperscalers raised funds there and Japanese investors' money financed a build-out elsewhere.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: Russia kept its key rate at 14%, a high return that supports holding rubles. Elsewhere, Witkoff met Putin as Trump pressed Ukraine to cut a peace deal, and Russia extended its diesel export ban after strikes on the Ufa refinery. None of these reports ties the exchange rate to any of it.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: South Africa's recent news ran to a budget that cuts the fuel levy until January 2027, a judge voiding R12.6 billion in antiretroviral drug awards, and local elections with 73% of those surveyed trusting councils little or not at all. None of it accounts for the price.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: The worst of the slide coincided with the theft of $6.3 billion from Binance, which the FBI blamed on North Korea's TraderTraitor. Binance says it has refilled 90% of the stolen funds, a claim that remains unaudited, and when withdrawals reopened, users took out a net $3.64 billion.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: The low came as Binance froze funds after a $6.3 billion theft the FBI blames on North Korea's TraderTraitor. Withdrawals reopened and customers pulled a net $3.64 billion. Days earlier, the US Senate fell short of the 60 votes the Clarity Act needed, and the bill stalled.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Higher oil is pushing up US inflation, and that has traders betting on a Fed hike, which hurts a metal that pays no interest. The World Bank expects global oil supply to fall 5.2% in 2026. Gold lost 3.6% in one October week, its worst since June, and edged lower again when the Fed held rates with limited guidance.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: An AI-spotted PHP flaw took websites down, Anthropic's IPO filing warned its AI could blackmail people, and Alphabet's capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion as Amazon's 12-month cash burn hit a record $42.4 billion. All of that came after the mid-October spike, and none of it explains it.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Putin met Trump's envoy Witkoff as Trump pressed Ukraine to cut a peace deal. Ukraine's General Staff then counted 54,400 Russian casualties in October, its own monthly record, and Novaya Gazeta, which lost 6 reporters to killings, is shutting. None of these stories dates from the early-October peak, so they do not explain it.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guards have claimed mine blasts on tankers using what they call unauthorised routes, while UK monitors said a boat crew attached 2 explosives to one tanker; over 30 attacks hit ships near Hormuz in October. TASS reported Iran would reopen the strait within 2 days of a deal, and Qatar's gas carrier Al Mayeda was hit.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Over 30 attacks hit ships near Hormuz in October, a record, and limpet mines disabled a tanker there. The IRGC Navy says tankers on an unauthorized route exploded on mines, a claim that warns shippers off any passage Tehran has not approved. Three days of talks in Doha produced no deal, and Brent hit $117.56.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthis claimed strikes on a Saudi pipeline and refinery and attacked Aden, while China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea and a Qatari gas tanker crossed it toward Poland. None of these reports names an attack on a ship in the strait or accounts for the vessel count.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The fortnight's Red Sea news was political rather than commercial: China and Djibouti backed free navigation there, Burhan offered Russia a Red Sea economic zone, TASS reported, and 14 Indian nationals were reported safe after a yacht attack off Yemen. None of it accounts for the canal's traffic.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's reporting carried nothing that accounts for traffic in this strait. The nearest shipping news came from Hormuz, where limpet mines disabled a tanker and the Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit, while Saudi Arabia agreed to store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Taiwan's map showed 53 Chinese ships, 34 of them warships, in a report published after the latest traffic reading. It says nothing about commercial shipping and does not account for the drop in traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones sank the Khoryv off Romania, killing 1 sailor, then the Contship Jet off Bulgaria, whose 18 crew survived. Erdogan condemned the attacks, Zelensky says Turkey will help restore Ukraine's grain corridor, and Rubio sees growing interest in a Black Sea ceasefire. None of it accounts for the strait's traffic.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Rubio saw growing interest in a Black Sea ceasefire, and Zelensky said Turkey would help restore Ukraine's grain corridor, but neither development accounts for the traffic through this strait.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight's news from Türkiye was diplomatic and strategic rather than financial: the Makkah defence pact, Istanbul hosting Iran mediators, a partnership with Canada and a floating gas platform for the Sakarya field, and none of it accounts for the price.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's 2027 budget continued its fiscal consolidation, and Binance entered talks for a licence after a five-year absence, but neither accounts for the price.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: The threat of a downgrade from MSCI set off the rout: Jakarta stocks fell 11.6% on a single Friday, their worst day since 1998. Indonesia later announced new measures to improve stock market transparency.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Worries about AI drove a tumble in Tokyo's tech stocks, and those shares pulled the index down with them. The same doubts lifted the yen as a safe haven, taking it to a one-month high at 156.28 per dollar.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Hong Kong's regulator froze HK$4.38 billion of IPO money over suspected faked public-offering demand, and humanoid robot maker Noetix reportedly filed to list in the city. China's third-quarter earnings split, with tech profit up 140% and property losing 53.2 billion yuan. None of this accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: China's blue-chip index fell 11 weeks straight, a record, and third-quarter earnings split by sector: tech profit rose 140% while property lost 53.2 billion yuan. Strong results did not protect shares, with Contemporary Amperex falling 15% despite a 21.2 billion yuan quarterly profit. New export orders fell to 48.7 in October.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Elice closed 30% below its offer price in Seoul amid doubts over AI data centres, and SK hynix cancelled a Solidigm listing worth up to $15 billion. South Korea then reported 1% quarterly growth, 3x the forecast, on the AI boom. None of these reports accounts for the index's swings.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The fortnight's big Mumbai stories were the debut of Jio Platforms after India's largest initial public offering, and likely central-bank dollar sales that lifted the rupee to 95.02. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Indonesia reduced its gas supplies to Singapore, which generates up to 95% of its electricity from gas, citing domestic energy needs, and Singapore's top envoy visited after the cuts; Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, will store crude in the Jurong caverns from 2027. None of this accounts for the price.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's news from Taiwan was of 53 Chinese ships, 34 of them warships, on Taipei's map, and a strike over bonuses by one of Micron's two Taiwan unions; none of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Australia was reported set for a fifth rate hike as its inflation fight intensified, and the car attack on MP Helen Haines in Wangaratta led the country's news, but nothing reported ties either event to this index.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's fortnight brought a fuel levy cut lasting until January 2027 and a judge voiding R12.6 billion in antiretroviral drug awards, but neither accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Lula overturned a first-round deficit to beat Flávio Bolsonaro, the market's pick, and Brazil's Black Monday followed: real futures fell 10% and stocks slumped with the currency. Prices had already risen 4.62% in a year, breaching the inflation ceiling, and companies had moved into dollar stablecoins before the vote.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Mexico's inflation hit 3.62% in early October, above forecasts, and Pemex posted a $573 million loss even as oil prices surged. Neither accounts for the index's path over these weeks.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Alberta voters rejected independence from Canada in a victory for Carney, Trump cut 50% tariffs on Canadian crates, boxes and seaweed, and gasoline helped push inflation to 3.1%. None of these reports ties any of it to the index's path, so the cause of its moves remains unexplained here.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The selloff ran through big tech's AI bills: Alphabet's capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion in one quarter and its cash flow turned negative, while Amazon's 12-month cash burn hit a record $42.4 billion. Intel lost 23% after hours despite beating revenue guidance, and the Fed's hold left markets fully pricing a December rate hike.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The fortnight's news from London centred on banks and the budget: HSBC's pretax profit hit $9.6 billion, Barclays paid shareholders £500 million while cutting 5,000 jobs, and the UK Budget set the tax burden on course for a record 38.6% of income. None of it accounts for the price.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The fortnight's German news pulled in opposite directions: Ifo expectations rose to 91.6 from 90.4, Volkswagen planned to freeze pay for 660,000 workers until 2030, and loan obstacles hit 7% of euro zone firms. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: France's own finances are the backdrop: long-term yields went from 4% in August to above 5%, with the 10-year reaching 4.96%, the highest since 2002. School protests became a cost-of-living revolt, with more than 500 arrests on the third weekend of riots, and Fitch cut its outlook after the economy shrank 0.1%.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Customers are asking ASML for lithography tools as far out as 2029 and 2030, and forecasters now see euro zone inflation averaging 3.0% this year. Neither story accounts for the index's path.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's fortnight was dominated by the Toledo train collision that killed at least 68 people, floods that cut off the east of the country and a Madrid march of 25,000 demanding pensions that keep pace with inflation. None of these accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's main news for Milan's banks was the ECB clearing Intesa Sanpaolo to bid €32 billion for Monte dei Paschi, while ECB policymakers brought a rate hike debate into the open. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The fortnight's Swiss market news was the first spot bitcoin ETF on SIX and a nine-month SNB profit on foreign currencies and gold, and neither accounts for the index's price.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Sweden's central bank revived its e-krona debate as stablecoins and a digital euro loom, but that argument over money does not account for the price of these shares.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: Israel's election left neither bloc with a majority unless it relies on Arab parties. Days later, Khamenei ordered commanders to answer any attack without geographic limits, and ship attacks near Hormuz hit a record in October. None of these reports links either event to the price of Israeli shares, so they do not account for the index's move.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Prosecutors revived a closed 2016 leak case against Comey, charging him a third time, while Trump called for a metal detector for Senate candidate El-Sayed. A day later, Trump aide Simon Levy confirmed political asylum in the US for Flávio Bolsonaro, who fled Brazil after losing to Lula.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Under Warsh, the Fed held rates despite intensifying inflation, and markets now fully price a December hike. Before the decision, TD Securities expected 3 dissents against the hold. The cost of keeping rates high already shows on bank balance sheets: Bank of America's unrealized bond losses rose to $109 billion.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour, its highest since 2022, and forecasters now see euro zone inflation averaging 3.0% this year, while households expect 3.1%. Panetta said more hikes may be needed even as loan obstacles hit 7% of firms. Christine Lagarde leaves on 7 February 2027, so her successor inherits the argument.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: Reporting in late October tied a US jobs pickup to the Fed staying on track to hike rates again, but it does not account for this rate's path.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Gold fell through the same days on a firmer dollar before the Fed decision, a hold with limited guidance, then higher oil and US inflation data that bolstered Fed hike bets. Metals that pay no interest lose appeal when rates look set to rise. Those reports concern gold, and none of them names silver.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: The Fed left interest rates unchanged despite the inflation, and gold then slipped as higher oil and US inflation data bolstered bets on a Fed hike. Those reports show what the figures set off in markets, but none of them accounts for why prices rose.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Over 30 attacks hit ships near Hormuz in October, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards say tankers on an "unauthorized route" exploded on mines, a warning to any shipper sailing without Tehran's approval. A US blockade of Iran runs alongside it. In Doha, Iran offered to reopen the strait within 2 days of a deal.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The Saudi-Houthi war reached Aden, where Houthis attacked and said Saudi strikes killed 16, while China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea. None of these reports describes an attack on shipping or a rerouting, so they do not account for the container traffic.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The fortnight's reports centred on the war between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, from a claimed Saudi pipeline strike to the threat against Riyadh's airport and the fighting in Aden, but none of them addresses canal traffic or accounts for these transits.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Trump pressed Kyiv to make a deal as his envoy Witkoff met Putin, and the Kremlin then asked for a seat for Europe at the talks while Lavrov predicted escalation. Ukraine's General Staff claimed 54,400 Russian casualties in October, a monthly record, and its air alert app was hacked into sending false radiation warnings.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple launched M6 MacBook Pro and iMac models, the Pro with a touchscreen and up to 24 hours of battery, while its foldable iPhone drew reports of growing pains. Alibaba's Qwen is also coming to Chinese iPhones. None of these reports accounts for the share price.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Alphabet's capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion in one quarter, and its free cash flow turned negative. A share is a claim on future cash, so a quarter in which the AI build-out consumed more than the business generated reaches the price directly.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon's AI spending pushed its 12-month cash burn to a record $42.4 billion, the sharpest of the pain points in its earnings. The figure arrived in a tech earnings season already eroding enthusiasm for AI, which turned attention from what the buildout might earn to the cash leaving to pay for it.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Microsoft offered buyouts to around 60,000 employees to contain costs while forecasting $175 billion in capital spending this year, setting payroll savings beside its AI push. It also dropped an AI data centre at Loughton, leased through Nscale, after grid power there slipped by as much as a decade.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX poured profit into AI, spending $16.4 billion on infrastructure last quarter and borrowing $40 billion for GPUs, mostly callable debt. In Ukraine, officials said Starlink cuts out at 130 km/h, and the Pentagon inspector general declined a nine-senator probe. Nothing here ties either story to the share price.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta ended the quarter $2.12 billion cash-negative on AI spending, then moved to raise $95 billion in stock for data centres, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom eyeing up to $5 billion of it. New nonvoting shares had already left an overhang Wall Street wants gone, and New Mexico fined the company $25 billion over Cambridge Analytica.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: A Houthi drone strike near the Shaybah field sent Brent to $110.63, and Saudi Arabia said it will store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027. Neither event accounts for the movement in Aramco's shares.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Net profit fell 43% to $787 million in the third quarter, and the same day brought word that SpaceX and Tesla were exploring a merger. Barclays has since called a merger a key part of the bull case for the shares, and one headline put the gain to Elon Musk at $100 billion.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung's earnings, alongside Alphabet's, rattled technology shares on Oct 29. Separately, it listed its fridges and washing machines in Hong Kong as sold out and is reportedly ending home appliance sales there, part of a wider China retreat, though nothing ties that exit to the share price.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: One of Micron's two unions in Taiwan struck at Taoyuan as a dispute over bonuses escalated. Nothing reported about the walkout, or anything else about the company's own business, accounts for the share price.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.
co:lilly.recent: Eli Lilly joined Walmart and 36 others in objecting to tokenized versions of their shares on OKX and ICE, and Belgium refused to cover Mounjaro, but neither accounts for the price.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Nigeria's central bank gave JPMorgan approval-in-principle to set up a merchant bank, the first licensing step for a firm in Lagos since 1961. A step that small in one market does not account for the price of the share.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: SK hynix cancelled a Solidigm listing worth up to $15 billion, at a time when its own record US listing was trading underwater. Neither report accounts for the swings in the Seoul share price.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: Walmart and Eli Lilly joined 36 others objecting to tokenized versions of their shares on OKX and ICE. The dispute concerns how the stock is traded rather than the retail business, and it does not account for the share price.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: Lithography tools are selling out, and customers are now asking ASML for machines to be delivered in 2029 and 2030. That demand was reported from Eindhoven, but nothing in the past fortnight's news accounts for the share price's moves.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.
ez-cpi.recent: Forecasters now see euro zone inflation averaging 3.0% this year, and the latest reading was reported as a three-year high. Neither report says what pushed prices up.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: Solana began charging 1 SOL per bug report after AI-generated spam helped swamp its $1 million bug contest with 809 reports. That changes how the network handles security submissions, and it does not account for the token's fall.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: Ripple won final approval for its U.S. national trust bank, putting its $2.5 billion stablecoin under a federal regulator, and XRP did not follow. Traders were leaving altcoins for bitcoin, which then dipped below $80,000 before the Binance hack sent it and ether tumbling. The XRP Ledger's bug fix also slipped to November after validator support dipped.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: Hyperliquid drew notice as the offshore venue where traders bet at 10-fold leverage on Anthropic's initial public offering, a contract out of reach on United States exchanges. That story concerns what trades on the platform, and nothing reported accounts for the token's price.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: CoinDesk's market reports logged one-day ZEC jumps of 11% and 8% in late October, beside Bitcoin's moves on AI earnings and ahead of a Fed decision, but neither headline gives a reason specific to Zcash, and nothing here accounts for the price.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: Bank of England policymaker Greene said inflation risks are bigger than thought, and gas explained £161 of a £180 rise in a UK bill. Inflation and borrowing data also framed the chancellor's Budget challenge. None of this accounts for the earlier cuts that brought the rate to its current level.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: Borrowing costs are at a 31-year high, and the two officials closest to the question framed inflation differently: finance minister Katayama said Japan was shifting to a wage-driven inflation phase, while BOJ chief Ueda said the 2% goal was not yet sustainably achieved. Foreign issuers, meanwhile, sold a record $16 billion of yen bonds.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: China's central bank spent the fortnight on market plumbing, not the price of credit: the PBOC plans a bond liquidity backstop that lends to funds, not just banks, and is piloting onshore yuan trade for foreign banks. Neither step accounts for the rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia held its key rate in October, with high inflation expectations a point of concern and, by its account, rising export revenues backing the ruble. It also kept buying yuan through the month. None of that accounts for the earlier cuts that brought the rate down.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Southeast Asians were scaling back weddings as inflation and an energy crisis took their toll, while the truce between Cambodia and Thailand remained under scrutiny. Neither story accounts for the price.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Saudi output had already sunk to a record 6.24 million barrels daily, a direct hit to an Aramco-heavy index, when Houthi attacks reached Shaybah and, by their claim, the East-West pipeline. Riyadh airport halted flights and the investor summit slipped to 2027. The defence minister then met Iran's president in Tehran.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: Bank of China's 2 billion yuan bond drew 5 times demand in Dubai, the UAE and Greece announced $14.3bn in deals, and Adnoc told clients its new Hormuz bypass pipe would start in early 2027. None of it accounts for the price.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Philippine inflation reached 7.2% in September against a 2-4% target, and the central bank answered with a half-point rate rise, raising the cost of money for the domestic borrowers and shoppers this market depends on. Oil above $110 after a Houthi drone strike near the Saudi Shaybah field added to the energy bill, and the peso stayed weak.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: A New Mexico case ended with Meta owing $25 billion over 43 million deception violations tied to Cambridge Analytica. Free cash flow then fell to negative $2.12 billion on AI spending, and new nonvoting shares created an overhang Wall Street wanted gone. Meta followed with a $95 billion stock offering, its largest ever, to pay for AI data centres.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The world's largest software company, maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and OpenAI's biggest backer. Its share is among the heaviest weights in US indices, so index funds worldwide move with it.
stocks:MSFT.recent: Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees while forecasting $175 billion in capital spending this year. It also dropped Nscale's AI site at Loughton, where grid power may wait a decade. None of these reports ties either decision to the share price.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent spent the fortnight on AI and video products: a preview of its Hunyuan Hy4 model, 2,000 free monthly search calls for developers, and the Lvpaopao short-drama service, which QuestMobile counted at 143 million monthly users in August. None of it accounts for the fall in the share price.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: Amazon pledged €16 billion in Germany for data centers and Prime, part of a build-out that has made AI its heaviest cash drain. Its 12-month cash burn hit a record $42.4 billion, a figure reported on Oct 30, after the last reading here, so it does not account for the earlier slide.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company founded by Elon Musk. It launches most of the world's orbital payloads on reusable Falcon rockets and runs Starlink, the satellite internet network that supplies most of its revenue.
stocks:SPCX.recent: SpaceX's revenue doubled last quarter, but its AI capital spending tripled, with $16.4 billion going to AI infrastructure, and it has borrowed $40 billion for GPUs, mostly callable debt. Musk himself warned of a neocloud shakeout. Nothing reported directly ties any of this to the share price.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win both the Senate and the House in the 2026 US midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which would give one party control of legislation and confirmations.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom eyed up to $5 billion of Meta's $95 billion stock sale, which would bankroll its AI push. Google's Nvidia chip challenge lifted its cloud sales, and iFlytek said it trained Spark X2.6 without Nvidia. None of this accounts for the share price.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is the world's largest oil exporter and the guardian of Mecca and Medina. It counts how many people looked the country up, not what happened there.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: The Houthis claimed strikes on a Saudi pipeline and a refinery and declared Riyadh airport a military target, while saying Saudi strikes killed 16 people. Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran, Egypt's parliament voted to defend the kingdom, and 2 of 3 signatories ratified the Makkah defence pact.

poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US, Russian and Chinese leaders meet together in person before 2027. A three-way meeting would put Beijing at the table on matters Washington and Moscow usually settle between themselves.
poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.recent: Trump's envoy Witkoff met Putin as Trump pressed Ukraine to cut a peace deal, but nothing reported in this period mentions Xi or a three-way meeting, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-ex-cuba-leader-raul-castro-in-us-cu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother, Cuba's president from 2008 to 2018 and party chief until 2021, is in US custody by year's end. Traders bet on Washington getting him before an American court.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Alphabet's quarterly results did the damage: search woes caused a revenue miss, while capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion and turned cash flow negative. Google admitted AI search makes less money and offered more ads as the fix. Its challenge to Nvidia in chips lifted cloud sales, but that same push crimped cash flow.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: Bets against a truce tracked the fighting: drone debris killed two near a Saudi oilfield and Saudi air defences intercepted 10 ballistic missiles. Diplomacy opened in parallel when Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran, and the coalition then said it shot down a Houthi drone near Mecca, which the Houthis denied.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Vance wrote to Iran's security chief Rezaei, and Qatari-mediated talks opened in Doha, where Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 2 days of a deal. Three days produced none. Netanyahu pressed Trump to strike after the midterms, sources say, and Iranian state news agency Mehr reported parliament would unanimously quit the nuclear treaty.

stocks:300750.SZ.standing: Contemporary Amperex Technology, the Ningde company listed in Shenzhen and the world's largest maker of electric-vehicle batteries. Carmakers from Tesla to BYD's rivals buy its cells, so its share tracks the EV and grid-storage build-out.
stocks:300750.SZ.recent: Contemporary Amperex reported a quarterly profit of 21.2 billion yuan, and its shares still fell 15% as China's tech stocks repriced. The earnings did not shield the company from the wider selloff.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats control the US Senate after the 2026 midterm elections. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet officers, so whoever holds it decides who a president can appoint.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: A federal judge dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking to halt certification of Mary Peltola if she wins in Alaska, and Senator Dan Sullivan vowed to honour the outcome. That settled one fight over one Senate seat; nothing reported here explains the wider rise in what traders will pay.

poly-bank-of-mexico-decreases-interest-r.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Banco de México cuts its overnight rate by a quarter point after November. That rate sets borrowing costs across Mexico and the yield gap that draws foreign money into the peso.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.
poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.recent: Venezuelans marched in Caracas on Thursday demanding a presidential election date, the one development in the fortnight's reporting that bears directly on this contract. The march came before the contract's later slide, and nothing reported since accounts for that fall.

poly-us-iran-ceasefire-continues-through.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the ceasefire between the United States and Iran survives until the US midterm elections. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, threats and mediation.
poly-us-iran-ceasefire-continues-through.recent: Axios's sources say Netanyahu pressed Trump to strike Iran immediately after Tuesday's midterms, while Trump for now wants negotiations to play out; a strike after the vote falls outside this contract. Three days of Qatari-mediated talks in Doha produced no deal, and the Revolutionary Guards claimed 2 tankers hit mines in Hormuz.

stocks:000660.KS.standing: South Korea's second-largest chipmaker and one of the world's two biggest makers of memory chips. It leads in high-bandwidth memory, the stacked DRAM beside AI accelerators, so its shares trade on AI data-centre spending.
stocks:000660.KS.recent: SK hynix shelved a listing of Solidigm, its NAND storage arm, that would have raised up to $15 billion, while its own record US listing was trading underwater. Most of the slide came before that decision, and nothing in the input about the company's own business accounts for it.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-texas-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins Texas's US Senate race in November 2026. Texas has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988, so the price shows how far traders bet against that record.

poly-cuban-regime-falls-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Cuba's communist government loses power before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, set against a one-party state that has outlasted decades of US sanctions.

wiki-flavio-bolsonaro.standing: The daily readership of the Wikipedia article on Flávio Bolsonaro, the Rio de Janeiro senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who carries his father's movement on Brazil's right.
wiki-flavio-bolsonaro.recent: Lula overturned a first-round deficit to beat Flávio Bolsonaro by 4.4 million votes in the runoff, an upset that sent real futures down 10%. Bolsonaro then left Brazil through no regular border post, a police official said, and Trump aide Simon Levy confirmed political asylum in the US. Lula called the flight 'shameful'.

stocks:JPM.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, spanning Chase's consumer branches, corporate lending and one of Wall Street's biggest investment banks. Its results are read as a check on American borrowers.
stocks:JPM.recent: JPMorgan, in Lagos since 1961, won approval-in-principle from Nigeria's CBN to set up a merchant bank, the first step in licensing, though that decision does not account for the share price.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.
poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.recent: Tinubu launched his re-election bid in Kaduna with petrol at about 1,400 naira a litre, and Microsoft pledged to load Nigeria's candidate list into its AI systems. Neither story concerns Peter Obi, and neither accounts for the price of this contract.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: What traders on Polymarket pay for a contract that settles at 100 if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate race. Ohio has leaned Republican in recent statewide contests, so the seat bears on which party controls the Senate.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win a majority in the US House of Representatives at the 2026 midterm elections. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and House control decides whether a president's agenda can pass.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The fortnight's midterm news was fought in court, not over House seats: former FBI officials were charged over 2023 testimony, and a federal judge dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking to halt certification of Mary Peltola in Alaska. Neither accounts for what traders will pay on this contract.

poly-netanyahu-out-before-2027-684-719-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu stops being Israel's prime minister before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with coalition crises, court cases and election timing.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

wiki-benjamin-netanyahu.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister. It rises with his elections, wars and trials, which have shaped Israel's politics for three decades.
wiki-benjamin-netanyahu.recent: Israel voted on Tuesday, with polls putting Eisenkot 8 to 10 points ahead of Netanyahu, and neither bloc reached 61 seats without Arab parties. Netanyahu then claimed fraud by Arab voters; Shin Bet said its probe does not implicate them and that they voted legally.

stocks:AMD.standing: A Santa Clara chip designer selling x86 processors for PCs and servers and Instinct accelerators for AI data centres. Its shares price how much AI spending buyers will steer away from Nvidia.

poly-will-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva-win-.standing: A Polymarket parlay that pays only if three separate things happen: Lula wins Brazil's presidency, Gadi Eisenkot becomes Israel's prime minister, and Democrats take the US Senate. If any one leg fails, it pays nothing.
poly-will-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva-win-.recent: Israel's vote supplied one leg: turnout among Palestinian citizens threatened Netanyahu, and neither bloc reached 61 seats without Arab parties, leaving Eisenkot's path to the premiership running through them. In the Senate race, filings showed Mike Rogers's spokesperson is a registered agent for Israel. Nothing reported explains the Lula leg.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Pakistan, the nuclear-armed South Asian state of more than 240 million people. It shows when world events send people looking for the country's basics.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Tehran told army chief Asim Munir that no enriched nuclear material will leave Iran, as Pakistan joined Saudi and Turkish officials in talks to head off a fresh assault. At home, diesel passed Rs400 a litre, flour reached Rs150-170 a kilo and retired officials warned against a constitutional amendment. None of it dates from the mid-October peak.

stocks:002230.SZ.standing: A Hefei-based maker of speech-recognition and AI software, listed in Shenzhen, whose Spark models sell into Chinese schools and government. On the US entity list since 2019, it is a test of building AI without American chips.
stocks:002230.SZ.recent: iFlytek said it trained its Spark X2.6 model on domestic chips, without Nvidia, and that one training run fell from 4.5 months to 1.2. For a company shut out of American hardware by export controls, that bears directly on its business: it can keep building models on chips it is allowed to buy.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: South Korea's largest company and one of the world's biggest makers of memory chips, smartphones and displays. It carries so much weight in Seoul's stock market that its share price moves the national index with it.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: Samsung is pulling fridges and washing machines out of Hong Kong months after quitting the mainland Chinese appliance market, keeping TVs and phones as Chinese brands take white goods. The share answers to memory chips instead: that business lifted it about 8% in a week before Thursday's earnings selloff on the Kospi.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire by the end of November 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each round of talks and each wave of strikes.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Trump pressed Ukraine to cut a deal and Witkoff met Putin, but no agreement followed, and the day before bets on a ceasefire hit their cheapest, Lavrov said the war would continue and likely escalate. The one truce that did hold was a four-hour window for evacuating Oleshky.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Bets on a truce climbed as Trump's envoy Witkoff met Putin and Trump pressed Ukraine to cut a deal. Then Lavrov said the war would continue and likely escalate, and the Nordic leaders' call with Putin drew criticism from EU partners. The only truce on the ground was a four-hour window to evacuate Oleshky.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares of the Cupertino maker of the iPhone, Mac and iPad, one of the world's most valuable listed companies. The iPhone earns most of its revenue, and its products are assembled largely in China on chips made in Taiwan.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple put its M6 chip in a new MacBook Pro and iMac, bringing a touchscreen and OLED to the Mac and claiming 24 hours of battery from $1,999. Its foldable iPhone, meanwhile, drew reports of growing pains and a crease. Alibaba's Qwen is also coming to Chinese iPhones through Apple Intelligence, news that arrived after the chart's last close.

stocks:ISP.MI.standing: Italy's largest bank by assets, listed in Milan, with a dominant share of the country's retail deposits and a big book of Italian government bonds, so its shares move with Italian sovereign risk.
stocks:ISP.MI.recent: The ECB gave Intesa Sanpaolo authorisation to take over Monte dei Paschi, clearing the way for a €32 billion bid. That approval came only this week, after the shares had already slid, and nothing else in the input explains the earlier fall.

stocks:002415.SZ.standing: The world's largest maker of video-surveillance cameras, listed in Shenzhen and controlled by state-owned CETC. US sanctions and Western bans on its gear in government sites limit what it can sell abroad.

stocks:BMPS.MI.standing: The Siena lender founded in 1472, the oldest bank still operating. The Italian state rescued it in 2017, and its fate has since been a test of how far Italy's banks will consolidate.
stocks:BMPS.MI.recent: The ECB authorised Intesa Sanpaolo to take over Monte dei Paschi, which clears Italy's largest bank to bid €32 billion for the Siena lender. The approval came at the end of the period, and nothing reported before it accounts for the share's earlier fall.

stocks:002236.SZ.standing: One of China's two largest makers of surveillance cameras and video systems, based in Hangzhou. US export blacklisting and an FCC equipment ban shut it out of American markets, so its sales lean on China and emerging markets.

stocks:000063.SZ.standing: China's second-largest telecom equipment maker after Huawei, based in Shenzhen and listed there and in Hong Kong. A 2018 US export ban nearly shut it down, so its shares move on Washington's rules on chips.

stocks:COIN.standing: The largest US cryptocurrency exchange, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from trading fees and custody, so its shares move with crypto prices and how much people trade.
stocks:COIN.recent: A vendor's breach exposed the contact details of a "small subset" of Coinbase customers, but that report is dated 2026-10-28, after the latest close on this chart, and nothing else here about the company's own business accounts for the fall.

stocks:AMPL.standing: Amplitude sells product-analytics software that records how people use apps and websites, so companies can see which features keep customers. Its subscription revenue rises and falls with corporate software budgets.
